intuition: Build the schedule by repeatedly taking a course with no unfinished prerequisites. After taking it, lower the requirement counts of courses that depend on it. This creates a valid order directly. If the order cannot include every course, a cycle makes a full schedule impossible.

Store outgoing edges from each prerequisite to its dependents and count each course’s unfinished incoming edges. Courses with zero incoming count are ready now, including courses unrelated to any prerequisite. Processing one ready course decreases the counts of exactly its dependents.

The queue produces a valid prefix because every emitted course has already had all prerequisites emitted. A cycle can leave a remaining group in which every course still waits on another. If processing stops before all courses are emitted, no complete valid order exists; returning a partial prefix would hide that impossibility.

steps: For four courses and pairs [[1,0],[2,0],[3,1],[3,2]], create edges 0→1, 0→2, 1→3, and 2→3.
The initial indegrees are [0,1,1,2], so only course 0 enters the ready queue.
Emit 0. Decrease the counts of courses 1 and 2 to zero, adding both to the queue.
Emit 1 next. Course 3 still has indegree 1 because prerequisite 2 is unfinished, so it does not become ready yet.
Emit 2, reducing course 3’s indegree to zero. Then emit 3.
All four courses were emitted, so return [0,1,2,3]. Swapping courses 1 and 2 would also be a valid answer.

codeNotes.note: The edge follows the direction of work unlocked after completion, not the opposite textual order of the input pair.
A dependent is ready only after every incoming obligation was removed, preventing premature scheduling after just one prerequisite.

codeNotes.code: return order if len(order) == numCourses else []
codeNotes.note: A shortened order indicates blocked cyclic dependencies. Reject the incomplete schedule rather than presenting its ready prefix as a full answer.

keyDecision: Return the order only when its length equals numCourses; otherwise return an empty list.

concept.question: How does removing finished prerequisites reveal the next ready courses?
intuition: Following prerequisites recursively can revisit the same requirements. The key question for each course is how many prerequisites are still unfinished.

Begin with courses that have no remaining requirements. Finishing one removes a requirement from each dependent course. A course becomes ready only when all its requirements have been removed. A directed cycle keeps its members waiting forever.
concept.observation: A dependent course becomes ready only when its remaining prerequisite count reaches zero.
approach: Count unfinished prerequisites for each course.
Take ready courses and remove their outgoing requirement obligations.
Return the completed order if requested, or whether all courses finish; a stalled incomplete process means a cycle.
concept.correctness: Each ready course has no unfinished prerequisites, so taking it respects all its constraints. Removing its requirements preserves the exact unfinished counts. If the process stalls with courses remaining, following an unfinished prerequisite backward in the finite remaining graph eventually repeats a node, exposing a cycle. Thus completion is equivalent to an acyclic feasible schedule.

complexity.explanation: Every course enters the ready queue once and every prerequisite edge is removed once. Work and graph storage are linear in courses plus requirements.

pitfalls: A dependent course becomes ready only when its remaining prerequisite count reaches zero.
Cycle members cannot release one another without an initial ready course.

scenes.title: Only course zero is initially ready
scenes.narration: Requirements are 0 before 1 and 2, then both 1 and 2 before 3. Initially only 0 has no unfinished prerequisites.
scenes.decision: Readiness means all requirements are finished, not merely one.

scenes.title: One prerequisite is still not enough
scenes.narration: Finishing 0 releases 1 and 2. Finishing 1 leaves course 3 still waiting for 2.
scenes.decision: Do not release a course after only one of several prerequisites.

scenes.title: The final requirement releases three
scenes.narration: Finishing 2 releases 3. All courses finish in order [0,1,2,3]. Return that order.
scenes.decision: Every emitted course has all prerequisites earlier in the order.
